label: Third original token when the second token is "f" (t=2, prev_tok=f)
explanation: Fires almost only at step t=2 of the original phase, when the token input at t=1 was f, whatever the current token is (99.9% of activation mass is at t=2). Strength depends on the first token: sequences starting "f f" give the maximum activation (1.0 of max); some first tokens such as 3 give high values (~0.75); others give low values (k, w: ~0.1-0.15); and sequences starting with z are mostly inactive (most of the false positives). Rare weak spillover at t=3 after "x f f". Never fires at t=0/1, at t>=4, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase, and never after any token other than f.

issues: Core predicate holds up on the test split: precision 0.987, recall 0.997, F1 0.992, mass recall 0.9995. The profile confirms 99.9% of activation mass at t=2 and zero activity at t=0/1, at t>=4, on the delimiter and in the copy phase.

Minor factual error: the explanation says sequences starting with z are 'mostly inactive'. Scoring (t==2)&(prev_tok==f)&(orig(0)==z) on test gives precision 0.64 (591 predicted). So z-initial sequences are mostly ACTIVE, just very weakly (mass recall 0.0012). They are still the main source of false positives (all 8 FP examples shown start with z f). Excluding z gives precision 1.0 but lowers F1 to 0.987, so the original predicate stays the best.

Spillover description is loose. The t=3 misses (46 on test, 0.0% of mass) come after '? f f' with various first tokens (t, g, 2), not specifically 'x f f'. Precision of (t==3)&(prev_tok==f)&(orig(1)==f) is only 0.08, so this is scattered noise, not a systematic class.

The magnitude claims are only partly checked. f f starts do give maximal activation (precision 1.0, mass share 6.3% from 3.4% of active steps). The miss renders show first token t at about 0.76 of max and g/2 at about 0.27-0.30, so other first tokens also give high values besides 3. Not contradictory, just incomplete.
